description:
FILED s532d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08), found as the FIRST cause of #4165's acceptance row (Template-Toolkit compile2.t 9).  PRE-EXISTING (base 06a4b8ba gives the same).

perl's utime takes ONE list: `my @t = (stat $g)[8,9]; utime(@t, $f)` sets $f's times from @t and returns 1.  PCL emitted `(p-utime @t $f)`, and p-utime's lambda list (&optional atime mtime &rest files) bound the ARRAY to ATIME, $f to MTIME and no file: 0 files touched, rc 0, no error.  #2923 had fixed the LIST half (`utime $a, $m, @files`); the times half was still positional.
Template Toolkit's compile2.t / compile5.t hack a compiled .ttc and restore its mtime with exactly `utime(@current_times, $compiled)`: under PCL the mtime stayed `now`, Template::Provider's _compiled_is_current (mtime ==) said stale, and the template was recompiled from SOURCE -- the hack was never read (and #4165, the module cache's mtime-only test, was the next cause behind it).

REPRO (perl 5.40.3 vs base): scratch/s532d/pr/ttc/ut.pl + ut2.pl in the s532d worktree:
    my @t = (1700000000, 1700000100); print utime(@t, $f), " ", (stat $f)[9];   # perl 1 1700000100, base 0 <now>
    utime((stat $g)[8,9], $f)   # perl 1, base 0
    my @all = ($at, $mt, $f, $g); utime(@all)   # perl 2, base 0

=== DONE (s532d) ===
FIX (cl/ only, emission IDENTICAL): p-utime re-splits the flattened argument list when either time slot is an aggregate spread (%p-utime-spread-p: an array, a hash, a list); the spread elements are VALUES, so an undef among them is time 0 (perl tests &PL_sv_undef identity, which only a literal undef is).  Guard: Pl/t/autodie-01.t row 13 (spread / stat slice / whole list in one array / a one-element array + a literal), inverse-verified on 06a4b8ba.  Acceptance: TT compile2.t 9 + compile5.t 8 12 pass (with #4165), left the board baseline by edit.
RESIDUE (pre-existing, NOT fixed, not filed separately -- one line here): `my $u; utime($u, $u, $f)` -- perl sets time 0 (a variable is not &PL_sv_undef), PCL sets `now`: a never-assigned `my $u` is a raw slot holding *p-undef*, the same value a literal undef emits, so p-utime cannot tell them apart.  The Pl/t/autodie-01.t row 12 spelling `my ($u, $v)` agrees with perl.
subject: utime(@t, $f) with the TIMES spread from an array touched nothing and answered 0 (p-utime took the array as ATIME) -- silent wrong; Template Toolkit compile2.t / compile5.t restore a .ttc's mtime this way
